title: Breath of Fire: Dragon Quarter
subtitle: An ascent from far below the surface
summary: Breath of Fire: Dragon Quarter is Capcom's PlayStation 2 role-playing game, first released in Japan on 14 November 2002. The fifth entry moves the series into an industrial underground world, where the journey proceeds upwards through bunkers and tunnels. Ryu's dragon power offers an extraordinary advantage but carries a limit that gives its use lasting consequences. The campaign becomes an attempt to reach the surface with the resources available. Its enclosed setting and unusual progression make this a deliberate change of direction from the earlier games' broader fantasy journeys.
body: Breath of Fire: Dragon Quarter is Capcom's PlayStation 2 role-playing game, first released in Japan on 14 November 2002. The fifth entry moves the series into an industrial underground world, where the journey proceeds upwards through bunkers and tunnels. Ryu's dragon power offers an extraordinary advantage but carries a limit that gives its use lasting consequences. The campaign becomes an attempt to reach the surface with the resources available. Its enclosed setting and unusual progression make this a deliberate change of direction from the earlier games' broader fantasy journeys.

Combat and exploration ask the player to consider what will still be available later in the ascent. Dragon abilities can solve an immediate danger while making the larger journey harder to complete. Ordinary battles therefore matter as opportunities to preserve that strength as well as earn progress. The underground map reveals nearby doors, enemies and treasure, giving preparation a practical role before an encounter. Instead of assuming that every resource can be restored after the next fight, the player must decide which problems justify using something difficult to recover.

The Scenario Overlay system makes restarting part of the design. Equipment, skills and other gains can carry into another attempt, while a higher D-Ratio opens additional scenes and areas. The player gradually understands more of the world while becoming better prepared to cross it. Makoto Ikehara directed the game, with Hitoshi Sakimoto composing its score. Dragon Quarter reached North America and Europe in 2003. Its unusual structure makes progress something larger than one uninterrupted playthrough: knowledge and preparation continue even when a particular attempt cannot reach the surface.
